newsitem.title: GERMANY: Blasts begin demolishing Berlin Nazi bunker.
newsitem.headline: Blasts begin demolishing Berlin Nazi bunker.

text.p: Demolition experts have begun blowing up a Berlin bunker which may have belonged to Adolf Hitler's armaments minister Albert Speer, but it could take up to 30 blasts to destroy it, an official said on Wednesday.

Each controlled blast can only be a weak explosion because the underground shelter is too close to landmarks like the Brandenburg Gate to risk shaking the sandy ground too much, a spokesman for a bank building on the site said.
The first detonation took place late on Tuesday evening, after the tourists who flock to the Gate, the nearby Reichstag parliament or the site of the former Berlin Wall were gone.

"We will have to knock down the bunker in several stages," said Christian Schilling, spokesman for DG Bank which will build a regional office on the Pariser Platz site between the planned new United States Embassy and the Academy of Fine Arts.
"Each explosion has to be rather weak so we don't harm any of the historic buildings around us," he said.
If the foundation of the Academy of Fine Arts weathers the shocks without damage, workmen could plan bigger blasts and speed up the demolition, he added.
Construction workers unearthed the bunker in December. Historians say it may have been used by Speer, who was Hitler's armaments minister and favourite architect.

Before the first blast, clean-up crews removed six and half tonnes of live and defused grenades and other ammunition along with cots, cutlery and telephones in the 225 square meter (2,400 square foot) subterranean complex.
Speer served Hitler until he slipped out of Berlin just before the end of the war. He was convicted of war crimes at the Nuremberg trials and sentenced to 20 years in prison.

Historians say the bunker could be one of at least six World War Two-era shelters under Pariser Platz, which is located near the former site of Hitler's chancellery and was once stranded in the no-man's land along the Berlin Wall.
